questions.question: ﻿Which scheme was launched by Indian government for creation of self employment opportunities for unemployed educated youth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Yojana.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Yojana** (PMRY) was launched by the **Indian government in 1993 **to create **self-employment opportunities **for **unemployed youth,** including educated youth.
 
• The scheme aimed to provide **financial assistance** to set up **small businesses or industries**, with a focus on the urban and rural poor.
 
• The scheme provided a maximum loan of **Rs. 2 lakhs** (now increased to Rs. 25 lakhs) at a concessional rate of interest to eligible beneficiaries.
 
• The beneficiaries were required to contribute a **small margin money **(5-10% of the project cost) and **undergo training **in **entrepreneurship development.**
 
• PMRY was merged with another scheme called the **Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme** (PMEGP) in** 2008,** which is currently being implemented by the **Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Rural Employment Guarantee Act **(NREGA) is a social welfare scheme that guarantees **100 days of wage employment** per year to rural households whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• **Annapurna scheme** is a **food security scheme **that provides food grains to eligible senior citizens who are unable to fend for themselves.
 
• **Grameen Udyami Yojana **is a scheme for providing **credit to rural entrepreneurs**, especially women, for setting up small businesses and industries.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Mauryan Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta Maurya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** was the founder of the **Mauryan Empire, **which was one of the largest empires in ancient India.
 
• He defeated the **Nanda dynasty** and established his own empire in **322 BCE.**
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was succeeded by his** son Bindusara** and later by his grandson **Ashoka**, who is known for his conversion to** Buddhism **and his efforts towards **promoting peace and non-violence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samudragupta **was a ruler of the** Gupta Empire**, which came after the **Mauryan Empire**.

 
 
• He is known for his military conquests and is often referred to as the **"Napoleon of India".**
 
 
 
• **Ashoka **was not the founder of the Mauryan Empire but was a significant ruler who expanded the empire and is known for his policies of** non-violence and religious tolerance.**
 
• **Chandragupta II **was a ruler of the **Gupta Empire **which came after the** Mauryan Empire**.
 
 
• He is known for his **military campaigns **and patronage of the arts.

questions.question:
Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu

This is an example of ________ reaction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**displacement.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction** Fe + CuSO₄ -> FeSO₄ + Cu** involves the **displacement of copper **from** copper sulfate **by **iron.**
 
• This is because **iron is more reactive** than copper and can displace it from its compound.
 
• This is an example of a **displacement reaction**, which is a type of** redox** (reduction-oxidation) reaction where there is a **transfer of electrons** between the reactants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neutralisation** reactions involve the** combination of an acid and a base** to form a salt and water. 
 
• **Reversible reactions** are those that can proceed in both the** forward and reverse directions.**
 
 
• The given reaction is **not reversible **as it proceeds in only one direction.
 
 
 
• **Iron** is a chemical element with the **symbol Fe** and atomic number **26.**
 
 
• **​**It is a **metal** and is found in many minerals, including** hematite and magnetite. **
 
• Iron is used in the **production of steel, **which is an important material in construction and manufacturing.

questions.question: Under the British colonial rule, India's economy was basically agricultural. At that time, approximately how many percent of the country's population was directly or indirectly earning their livelihood from agriculture?

• Approximately **85% of the population in India** relied on **agriculture** for their livelihood during the **British colonial rule.**

questions.question:
In the following example, who is the primary carnivore?

Grass-locust-frog-snake-hawk
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**frog.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Frog** is the** primary carnivore** in the given example.
 
• The term primary carnivore refers to an animal that primarily** feeds on other animals **for its survival.
 
• **Hawk **is also a** carnivore** but it primarily feeds on smaller animals like rodents and insects.
 
• **Grass** is a **plant** and not an animal, hence cannot be a carnivore.
 
• **Grasshopper** is a **herbivore** and feeds on plants, hence cannot be a carnivore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Snakes** are found in almost all parts of the world, except for** Antarctica, Iceland, Ireland, Greenland, and New Zealand.**

 
 
• There are more than **3,000 species** of snakes, and they vary in size from the **tiny thread snake,** which is only about **4 inches long,** to the reticulated python, which can grow up to **30 feet long.**
 
 
 
• **Hawks **are known for their **sharp eyesight, **which helps them to hunt their prey efficiently.
 
 
• They are also known to be **territorial and fiercely** defend their nests.
 
 
 
• **Grasshoppers** are known for their ability to** jump long distances**, thanks to their powerful hind legs.
 
 
• They are also a common food source for many animals, including** birds, rodents, and other insects.**

questions.question: What should be the minimum age for being a member of Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Minimum age** for being a member of **Lok Sabha is 25.**
 
• This is mentioned in** Article 84** of the Indian Constitution, which states that a person must be **at least 25 years old **to be a member of the Lok Sabha.
 
• **30 years **is the** minimum age** required to be a member of the **Rajya Sabha,** as mentioned in **Article 80 **of the Constitution.
 
• It is important to note that there are other **eligibility criteria **as well, such as being a citizen of India and not holding an office of profit under the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Lok Sabha **is the** lower house of the Indian Parliament**, consisting of members elected by citizens of India.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** is the** upper house** of the Indian Parliament, consisting of members elected by **state and territorial legislatures.**
 
• The Indian Constitution also provides for a minimum age of **35 years **for being eligible to be the **President of India (**Article 58), and a minimum age of **35 years **for being eligible to be the** Governor of a state (Article 157). **
 
• These age limits are important to ensure that individuals who hold important** positions of power and responsibility** have the necessary **maturity and experience** to discharge their duties effectively.

questions.question: ﻿Which of the following is an agriculture based industry?

• **India** is the **second-largest producer** of silk in the world after **China.**
 
• Silk is a** natural protein fiber** that is obtained from the **cocoons of silkworms.**

• The silk textiles industry involves various processes like rearing **silkworms, harvesting cocoons, reeling silk threads, spinning, weaving, and dyeing**.
 
• Silk textiles are popular for their **lustrous appearance, softness, and durability.**
 
• They are used to make a wide range of products like** sarees, dress materials, scarves, ties, and home furnishings.**
 
• Apart from silk, India is also a major producer of other natural fibers like **cotton, jute, and wool,** which form the basis of several other industries like textiles, handicrafts, and carpets.

questions.question: The _______ committee was set up to make recommendations about the fundamental duties.

• **Scheduled Banks **are those banks that are listed in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• These banks are eligible for **loans from the Reserve Bank of India** (RBI) at a** concessional rate of interest.**

• The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 is an important legislation that empowers the Reserve Bank of India to** regulate the banking sector** in India and **maintain financial stability i**n the country.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is the **country's central bank and regulatory body,** and it is in charge of policing the nation's banking industry.
 
• The Indian government's **Ministry of Finance** is the owner.
